source_text:
Fragmentum in epistulam ii ad Timotheum
637 2 Tim 2,2 Πιστοῖς ἀνθρώποις. ἤγουν ἐπισκόποις, πρεσβυτέροις, οὓς ἔμελλεν ὁ
Τιμόθεος χειροτονεῖν. ∆ιὰ πολλῶν μαρτύρων, τοῦτ' ἔστι νόμου καὶ προφητῶν.
thought_title: Faithful men are bishops and elders; witnesses are Law and Prophets
orientation: Photius comments on the lemma from 2 Timothy 2:2, explaining who the faithful men are and what the many witnesses mean.
pass_a_gloss: Faithful men. That is, bishops, elders, whom Timothy was about to ordain. Through many witnesses, that is, of the Law and the Prophets.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'faithful men'; banned alternatives are 'reliable men' and 'trustworthy people'.
Glossary votes for 'elders'; banned alternatives are 'presbyters' and 'priests'.
Glossary requires 'ordain'; banned alternatives are 'appoint' and 'consecrate'.
Glossary requires 'witnesses'; banned alternatives are 'martyrs' and 'testimonies'.

choices.english: of the Law and the Prophets
choices.why: Glossary requires 'the Law and the Prophets'; banned alternative is 'the Old Testament scriptures'.

pass_b_english: "Faithful men" (2 Timothy 2:2) — that is, bishops and elders, whom Timothy was about to ordain. "Through many witnesses" means through the Law and the Prophets.
